Laskarzew Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Łaskarzew, Poland

Demolished. Jews are recorded near Łaskarzew from the mid-18th century, though settlement bans delayed actual residency by about a century; by 1921, 1,251 Jews lived there, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery was likely established around 1863, when local Jews sought independence from Garwolin's synagogue district. In autumn 1943, German gendarmes shot roughly 45 people in the cemetery who had been caught hiding in nearby forests. Postwar, a Communist-era transformer station was built on the grounds; restoration in 1987-1988, led by local Holocaust survivor Zygmunt Warszawer, fenced part of the site and relocated tombstones from Sobienie-Jeziory. Since then the site has suffered renewed vandalism, including theft of Stars of David from the fence and graffiti on its Holocaust memorial.
